Formulation  
- Patient is an adult female with pre-existing chronic medical conditions (type 2 diabetes and hypertension) presenting with acute respiratory symptoms consistent with presumed viral chest infection. Symptoms include persistent dry cough, rhinorrhea, intermittent chills, and low-grade fever (not confirmed with thermometer). No reported psychological symptoms or concerns during consultation. Diabetes is a predisposing factor for increased risk of bacterial infection, warranting close monitoring. Social support is present (partner). No mental health issues identified or discussed.

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
  Topics Covered: Nature of viral chest infection, importance of temperature monitoring, signs to seek further medical attention (persistent fever >37.5-38°C, worsening cough with purulent sputum, hemoptysis, shortness of breath, chest pain, blood from nose), management of cough and avoid duplication of paracetamol with lemsip, diabetes and infection risk awareness.  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Persistent or worsening fever, increased cough severity, sputum production, blood in cough or nose, respiratory distress.  
- Coping Strategies: Symptomatic care with lemon sips, rest, hydration, temperature monitoring.
